analysis.subject: civics
analysis.pageCoverage: Introductory overview of Bill of Rights origins, Constitutional debate concerns, state convention demands, First Congress proposal of 12 amendments, and ratification outcomes including December 15, 1791 and May 7, 1992

overview.headline: From 12 proposed amendments to Bill of Rights ratified December 15, 1791

keyPoints.point: 12 amendments originally proposed and 10 ratified became Bill of Rights in 1791
keyPoints.quote: Although 12 amendments were originally proposed, the 10 that were ratified became the Bill of Rights in 1791.

keyPoints.point: opponents charged Constitution would open way to tyranny by central government
keyPoints.quote: its opponents repeatedly charged that the Constitution as drafted would open the way to tyranny by the central government

keyPoints.point: They demanded bill of rights to spell out immunities of individual citizens
keyPoints.quote: They demanded a "bill of rights" that would spell out the immunities of individual citizens.

keyPoints.point: First Congress proposed 12 amendments to Constitution on September 25, 1789 to state legislatures
keyPoints.quote: On September 25, 1789, the First Congress of the United States therefore proposed to the state legislatures 12 amendments to the Constitution

keyPoints.point: Articles 3 to 12 ratified December 15, 1791 by three fourths of state legislatures constitute first 10 amendments
keyPoints.quote: Articles 3 to 12, ratified December 15, 1791, by three-fourths of the state legislatures, constitute the first 10 amendments

keyTerms.gloss: first 10 ratified amendments that define citizens rights in relation to government
keyTerms.quote: Although 12 amendments were originally proposed, the 10 that were ratified became the Bill of Rights in 1791.

keyTerms.gloss: national authority under Constitution feared to impose tyranny if unchecked
keyTerms.quote: its opponents repeatedly charged that the Constitution as drafted would open the way to tyranny by the central government

keyTerms.gloss: protections for individual citizens spelled out as demanded rights
keyTerms.quote: They demanded a "bill of rights" that would spell out the immunities of individual citizens.

keyTerms.gloss: legislative body that proposed amendments for state legislatures to consider
keyTerms.quote: On September 25, 1789, the First Congress of the United States therefore proposed to the state legislatures 12 amendments to the Constitution

keyTerms.gloss: elected bodies whose ratification by three fourths made amendments part of Constitution
keyTerms.quote: Articles 3 to 12, ratified December 15, 1791, by three-fourths of the state legislatures, constitute the first 10 amendments
